clue.text: Banking controller in a role changed

indicators.note: letters that are changed have been moved into a different order

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone controlling a bank finds their job description altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' suggests finance, but it means an aircraft tilting as it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is the hinged flap on an aircraft wing that makes the plane roll, or bank, in a turn.

clue.text: Cider producer doubling pressure in beer

indicators.note: one item sitting in another is placed inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
P is the abbreviation for pressure, written twice

explanation.surface: A cider maker is doubling the pressure in the beer vats.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is pressed from apples, so the fruit is what produces it.

clue.text: The Leninist shot outside City in principality

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the outside of the other piece
something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters fall apart and regroup

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A Leninist gunned down outside a city in a small European state.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the financial district of London, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Liechtenstein is a tiny Alpine country ruled by a prince, hence a principality.

clue.text: Control report of wet weather

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: wet weather is rain, which is pronounced the same as the word for rule

explanation.surface: A weather forecast is in charge of reporting the wet spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule, which is to have control over a country.

clue.text: European in sauna developed queasiness

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed within it
something developed has been worked into a new form, so its letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European in a steam room starts feeling sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the sick feeling of wanting to vomit, which is queasiness.

clue.text: Animal taking the writer into California

indicators.note: the outer piece takes in the other one, holding it inside
the writer goes into the state abbreviation, sitting within it

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
the writer refers to the setter, who is me

explanation.surface: An author brings an animal along on a move to California.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a humped desert animal, a specific example of an animal.

clue.text: Fruit dessert to arrive without container

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the verb sits around the other piece

parts.note: to come is to arrive
a pot is a container

explanation.surface: A dessert is delivered with no dish to put it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Compote is fruit stewed in syrup and served as a pudding.

clue.text: Shiny layer from flap o' the ormer possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the given letters

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A shiny lining might come from the flap of an ormer shell.
explanation.walkthrough: An ormer is an abalone, a shellfish whose shell is lined with nacre, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl, or nacre, is the iridescent inner layer of certain mollusc shells.

clue.text: No song for a wake?

parts.note: surface reading: music unsuitable for a funeral vigil
setter's reading: a song meant to stop someone being awake, sung to send a child to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: A wake suggests the gathering after a death; it is really the opposite of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a soothing song sung to make a baby sleep rather than wake.

clue.text: Criminal locates impure silver perhaps

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A thief tracks down some debased silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is one example of a precious metal, alongside gold and platinum.

clue.text: French in luck having missed initial boost

indicators.note: the word misses its opening letter, which is dropped

parts.note: en is French for in
chance is luck

explanation.surface: A French person's luck runs out at the first hurdle.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to improve or increase, the verb sense of boost.

clue.text: Tosca for example works in Latin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Puccini's Tosca is a sung drama
second meaning: the Latin plural of opus, a work

explanation.walkthrough: Opus means work in Latin, and its plural gives the musical-drama word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is one example of a staged musical drama, and the same word is the Latin plural for works.

clue.text: Delight as property initially let

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of property
to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: A landlord is pleased to have a property let at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them pleasure, a synonym of the verb delight.

clue.text: Faint expression of petulance when idiot enters

indicators.note: one item enters another by going inside it

parts.note: a pout is a sulky face
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A faint sulky look appears when a fool walks in.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass out is to lose consciousness, which is to faint.

clue.text: Sild and roe prepared in private?

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the two fish words; and simply joins them

explanation.surface: Herring and fish eggs served as an army ration.
explanation.walkthrough: Sild are small herrings. 'Private' looks like an adjective; it is the lowest army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest-ranked soldier in the army.

clue.text: Clairvoyant touring London sees crime

indicators.note: a tour goes round a place, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: fey can mean having second sight
Lon is an abbreviation for London

explanation.surface: A psychic on a visit to London foresees a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A felony is a serious crime in legal terminology.

clue.text: Result of lob?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: a shot played up into the air

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, splitting the word into two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An upshot is the final outcome, and a lob, read jokily, is a shot that goes up.

clue.text: Girl around island back for crop producing fibre

indicators.note: going back means the whole result is read from right to left
the girl goes around the island, enclosing it

parts.note: a lass is a girl
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A girl walks round an island and comes back for a fibre crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is an agave plant grown for the tough fibre used in rope and matting.

clue.text: Airborne 12 preferred defensive feature

parts.note: 12 is the answer soldier; an airborne soldier is a paratrooper
a pet is a favourite or preferred one

explanation.surface: A paratrooper's favourite part of the fortifications.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12 points to the answer of 12-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective wall along a rampart, a feature built for defence.

clue.text: Clear others stashing MDMA

indicators.note: to stash something is to hide it away inside

parts.note: the rest are the others
MDMA is the drug ecstasy, known as E

explanation.surface: Other people are cleared despite hiding drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a device is to clear its settings back to the start.

clue.text: Tray emptied to hold rum drink

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the other piece between them
emptying a word removes its insides and keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of tray
rum means strange or odd

explanation.surface: A tray carrying a rum drink has been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' poses as the spirit but is the British adjective for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits, water, sugar and spices.

clue.text: Snog then it's off with brief amour

indicators.note: is off means gone wrong, so the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
and means along with

explanation.surface: After a kiss, the short romance is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of it's reads as is, and 'is off' is the anagram signal; snog is British slang for kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-night stand is a sexual encounter lasting a single night, a very brief affair.

clue.text: Singer a little overweight? Enormous!

indicators.note: a little means only a small part of the words that follow is taken

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A singer asks if they are slightly heavy and is told they are huge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, an example of a singer.

clue.text: To agree — completely!

parts.note: taken as written
two figures that tally agree

explanation.surface: An emphatic exclamation of complete agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally is an adverb meaning wholly or entirely.
